# Connectors (plugin)

`memwise/connectors` 1.0.0, first-party. No tools; two things:

1. **The connector setup guide** as a skill, `skills/connector-setup/SKILL.md` (a copy of the app's
   `sources.md`): how to set up an MCP server, an API or a local folder as a source, with its credentials.
2. **The bridge from sources to plugins.** Connectors people set up in chat are the workspace's *sources*
   (`<workspace>/sources/<slug>/`). Each enabled MCP source can be installed as a plugin of its own:

   ```yaml
   # generated by the app, one folder per source
   id: source/linear
   version: 1.0.0
   title: Linear
   trust: local
   mcp_servers:
     linear: { source: linear }
   ```

   The server `{ source: linear }` names the source, not its address or token. When a playbook calls one of
   its tools, the app resolves the source at call time (`resolveMcpSource`, in
   `packages/server-core/src/memwise/connectors.ts`): its command or URL from the source's config, and its
   credentials from the app's credential store. Nothing secret is written into the project folder, and a
   re-authenticated source is picked up on the next call.

   Its tools are found by connecting to the server at install (`tools/list`) and come in **unclassified**,
   like any MCP server's: until the binding classifies them they count as irreversible. Binding the plugin
   (the bind-plugin playbook) classifies them, maps its records onto domain entities, and freezes.

The app lists the sources it can install this way next to the example plugins ("Install a connector").
